chunks: Muhammad ibn Musa ibn al-Mutawakkhil (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated to us, saying: 'Ali ibn Ibrahim ibn Hashim narrated to us, from his father, from al-Abbas ibn 'Amr al-Fuqaymi, from Hisham ibn al-Hakam, that a man asked Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him)

whether Allah, the Blessed and Exalted, has pleasure and anger? He (peace be upon him) replied: Yes; however, it is not like what is found in created beings. This is because pleasure and anger are external intrusions that enter him, transferring him from one state to another, agitated, composite, with things having an influence in him. But our Creator has no influence of things in Him; He is One, One in Essence, and One in Meaning. His pleasure is His reward and His anger is His punishment, without anything intermingling with Him to stir Him up and transfer Him from one state to another. Indeed, that is the attribute of the helpless, needy created beings. He, the Blessed and Exalted, is the Powerful, the Honorable, who has no need of anything of what He created, and all His creation is in need of Him. He created things without any need or cause, by creation and innovation.
ai.seo_question: How does Shia theology distinguish between divine pleasure/anger and human emotions?
ai.summary: This hadith from Shaykh al-Saduq’s *al-Tawhid* articulates the Shia doctrine of divine simplicity, distinguishing Allah’s attributes from created beings by emphasizing that His pleasure and anger are intrinsic to His essence rather than transient emotional states. The Imam clarifies that while human emotions are 'intrusions' that alter one's state due to external causes, Allah’s pleasure is His reward and His anger is His punishment, reflecting His absolute self-sufficiency (al-Ghani) and lack of need for creation. This underscores the theological principle that divine attributes are not composite or subject to change, affirming His unique oneness in both essence and meaning.

en.sayed-ali-raza-rizvi: 3. Muhammad ibn Musa ibn al-Mutawakkil (may Allah be pleased with him) said: `Ali ibn Ibrahim ibn Hashim said, on the authority of his father, on the authority of al-`Abbas ibn `Amr al-Fuqaymi, on the authority of Hisham ibn al-Hakam, that a man asked Abu `Abdillah al-Sadiq (AS) whether Allah, the Blessed and Exalted, feels pleasure or anger.

Thus, he (AS) replied, Yes; however, it is not like the pleasure or anger found in created beings. Unlike human beings, pleasure and anger do not change Allah from one emotional state to another. Human beings are operated and composed. Things can affect human beings, while things cannot affect our Creator. He is One in Essence and Concept.
Thus, His Pleasure is His Reward, and His Anger is His Punishment, without anything interfering with Him so as to ridicule Him and transform Him from one sate to another. Emotional changes are an attribute of the created, the helpless, and the needy. While He, the Blessed and Exalted, is the Supreme and the Honorable, who has no need from any of His Creation although all of His Creation is in need of Him. Verily, He created everything without any need to create or innovate.
